subject: Argosy Labs — reserve structure, minimum GPUs, and onboarding cadence
messages:
From: Lara Simon <lara@argosylabs.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Tim Cole <tim.cole@argosylabs.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reserve options — what can we pick?

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving toward a reserved-capacity conversation on our side and need a compact set of options to present to the execs next Tuesday. High-level asks:

- A small set of 2–3 reserve structures (cluster size / min GPUs) that map to low/medium/high usage profiles.
- Clear ramp schedule (how fast capacity activates and when hard/soft decommits apply).
- What burst capabilities look like — can we burst cross-region for shorter windows?
- Any onboarding warm-up credits or reduced ramp pricing for the first 90 days.

We run a mix of batch embedding jobs (nightly) and low-latency chat inference during business hours. Peak concurrency for chat is ~60 rps (small prompts, mostly 2k tokens/session). Batch windows are ~3–4 hours nightly and spike token counts.

Can you send a short workbook with the options and a suggested activation timeline? We’d like to keep the exec ask to one slide.

Best,
Lara
Lara Simon
Head of ML Platforms, Argosy Labs
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Simon <lara@argosylabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve options — what can we pick?

Hi Lara — thanks, this is helpful context. Attached is a concise workbook (Argosy_Reserve_Options_v3.xlsx) with three tailored reserve profiles plus a 90‑day onboarding credit and suggested activation cadence. Summary below:

Option 1 — Foundational (low)
- Minimum GPUs: 8 A100-equivalent (serves baseline chat + nightly embed batch)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~30 rps chat + batch window handled with autoscaling to 12 additional burst GPUs
- Ramp: activate 25% at contract start, 100% by week 4; soft decommit allowed after 60 days with 30-day notice
- Warm-up: 200k free tokens and 50% reduced burst cost for first 30 days

Option 2 — Production (medium)
- Minimum GPUs: 24 A100-equivalent
- Sustained throughput: ~60 rps chat, batch windows without queuing; burst to +40 GPUs for nightly spikes
- Ramp: 50% at start, 100% by week 3; soft decommit gated to usage threshold (below 40% for 30 days)
- Warm-up: 400k free tokens + onboarding support (2x runbook calls)

Option 3 — Performance (high)
- Minimum GPUs: 48 A100-equivalent
- Sustained throughput: 120 rps chat; batch windows run concurrently without impact; burst +100 GPUs for short windows
- Ramp: immediate activation with phased traffic shaping over 2 weeks; narrower decommit windows (business negotiation)

Operational notes (short):
- Geo-bursting: supported for burst windows if you sign the multi-region SLA; cross-region routing adds ~8–15ms to tail latencies but preserves throughput during region outages.
- Caching & batching profile: we recommend enabling KV prefix caching for chat sessions and a batch-first queue for nightly jobs to reduce per-token cost. Workbook includes estimated token-level cost curves for your reported profile.
- Attachments: the workbook contains line-item pricing and a sample SLO paragraph for Dedicated customers.

I’ve cc’d Karthik for capacity confirmation and Marissa/Ben for commercial/legal items. Happy to compress this to a one-slide executive summary if you want — we can do that and a 30-minute sync tomorrow.

Regards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Argosy_Reserve_Options_v3.xlsx (workbook, 4 sheets)
From: Tim Cole <tim.cole@argosylabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Lara Simon <lara@argosylabs.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve options — what can we pick?

Thanks Irene — this looks great. A couple quick clarifications before we pull the slide together: 

1) For Option 2 (24 GPUs) — what is the minimum sustained token throughput you guarantee for chat at 95th p99 latency under 2s? Is that in the workbook?
2) For geo-bursting: is cross-region bursting a hard dependency on the multi-region SLA, or can we enable it as a temporary capability during incidents?
3) On the soft decommit language: we need a sample calendar-based example (how clauses apply if we drop from 24 to 10 GPUs for 2 months).

If you can point to the exact workbook cells for the throughput guarantees, that’ll speed the internal convo. Also please include a one-paragraph sample SLO we can drop on the slide (latency / uptime / region fallback).

On timing — we’re trying to finalize the ask by COB Monday (PST).

—Tim
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve options — what can we pick? (internal)

Internal notes / next steps:
- Karthik: confirm the 95th/99th throughput numbers for Option 2 and annotate workbook cells (done by 10:30 PT tomorrow).
- Marissa: prepare one-paragraph SLO (latency & region-fallback) and a short exec slide summarizing the 3 options and the recommended ask (finish by Monday COB).
- Ben: finance to draft the contract language for soft decommit example (calendar-based) and confirm if multi-region SLA can be toggled during incidents (assign to product/legal if needed).

Proposed reply to Tim/Lara: attach a single-slide summary and point them to cells B12:B18 in the workbook for the 95/99 throughput targets; add a short SLO paragraph (Marissa will supply) and an explicit calendar example for soft decommit.

I’ll sync with infra to validate burst limits across regions — if we can offer temporary cross-region burst without a full multi-region SLA, we should document latency delta and a short-term opt-in process.

-Karthik
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
